purpose: Permanent physical-logic policy for candidate V2 object-first prompts: object-first must not look like a human was digitally erased from an otherwise human-shaped scene. Applies catalog-wide to every V2-routed hobby regardless of archetype or containment rule.
rule_text: Do not solve a zero-human scene using invisible-human physics. Never show a tool, instrument, vessel, or object operating, pouring, swinging, or moving entirely on its own with no plausible physical cause - this reads as an erased person, not as an object-first composition.
forbidden_examples: a watering can pouring while floating unsupported in mid-air
a racket or bat swinging with no hand and no prior momentum shown
a musical instrument playing itself with keys/strings moving with no cause
a cup or kettle lifting or tilting itself
a tool (brush, pen, hammer, needle) actively working a material with no hand and no mechanism
chopsticks or utensils hovering as though invisibly held
allowed_causes_of_motion: gravity (a falling or dropped object, water pouring downward from a fixed spout under its own weight rather than tilting itself)
wind or air movement (fluttering pages, drifting dust, rippling fabric)
machine automation (a 3D printer head moving via its own mechanism, an automatic sprinkler, a self-stirring appliance)
a ball or object already in flight from a prior, unseen action
water settling or rippling after a very recent disturbance
a wheel, fan, or turntable spinning under its own established mechanism
rolling dice that have just been released (shown mid-roll or freshly settled, not being thrown by an invisible hand)
environmental aftermath (footprints, chalk dust, melting ice, steam) that does not require a currently-acting body
a mechanical or electronic process operating under its own established power source
compiler_integration_note: This policy is intended to be appended as a fixed, always-on section of the V2 base style (see global_style_v2_object_first.json's physical_logic_ref), immediately after the non-human-protagonist directive and before any per-hobby structural containment language, so it constrains every containment rule's scene design rather than being hobby-specific.
